elements.element: Cap is mutual (applies to each Party)
elements.evidence: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... The cap is mutual"

elements.element: Cap limb (a): fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim
elements.evidence: "the fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" (lowercase 'fees', not the illusory defined term, and no first-Order-Form or event anchor)

elements.element: Cap is the greater of the two limbs
elements.evidence: "shall not exceed the greater of (a) ... and (b) ..."
"neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages"
"Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of confidentiality"; cap and exclusion both open "Except for Excluded Claims"

elements.element: Uncapped carve-out: data protection and security obligations
Uncapped carve-out: infringement of the other party's IP
elements.evidence: "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property"

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not 'damages' for cap purposes
elements.evidence: "Customer's payment obligations are not damages and are not limited by this Section."

elements.element: Fallback: mutual cap of 12 months' fees
elements.evidence: greater-of cap includes "the fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"; "The cap is mutual"

elements.element: Fallback carve-outs: indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct
elements.evidence: "breach of confidentiality ... its indemnification obligations; gross negligence, wilful misconduct"

reasons: Operation 1 cures the illusory cap: it replaces the defined-term/first-Order-Form/event-anchored basis with the exact preferred greater-of structure (12 months' fees preceding the claim, or USD 1,000,000), and preserves mutuality and the 'Except for Excluded Claims' hook.

All preferred uncapped carve-outs (confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnity, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, other party's IP) and the mutual consequential-damages exclusion remain untouched and effective.

Operation 2 restates the payment-obligations sentence to the preferred formulation. Note that dropping 'undisputed' and 'for conforming Services' widens what sits outside the cap for Customer; this tracks the preferred wording but is the one edit where the original was already substantially at position, so a narrower tweak would also have sufficed.
No undefined terms, contradictions or dangling mechanics introduced; 21.2's direct-damages sentence and the Excluded Claims definition continue to operate.
